Algautr.desc: From the Old Norse elements alfr meaning "elf" and gautr meaning "Geat" (a North Germanic tribe).

Alger.desc: From a surname that was derived from the given name Algar.

Algernon.desc: Originally a Norman French nickname, derived from aux gernons "having a moustache", which was applied to William de Percy, a companion of William the Conqueror. It was first used a given name in the 15th century (for a descendant of William de Percy). This name was borne by a character (a mouse) in the short story Flowers for Algernon (1958) and novel of the same title (1966) by the American author Daniel Keyes.

Algimantas.desc: From Lithuanian alga "salary, pay" combined with mantus "intelligent" or manta "property, wealth".

Algirdas.desc: Possibly means "all-hearing", from the Lithuanian roots al- "all, every" and gird- "to hear". This was the name of a 14th-century Grand Duke of Lithuania.

Algis.desc: Short form of Algimantas, Algirdas and other names beginning with the same sound.

Alhaji.desc: Means "the pilgrim" in Hausa, a derivative of Arabic حَجّ (hajj) meaning "pilgrimage, hajj". It is typically a title, not a name.

Al-Hasan.desc: Form of Hasan prefixed with the Arabic definite article.

Alhassan.desc: Form of Al-Hasan used in western Africa.

Alheri.desc: Means "the charitable, the good" in Hausa, from Arabic خير (khayr).

'Ali.desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic عليّ (see Ali 1).

Ali 1.desc: Means "lofty, sublime" in Arabic. Ali ibn Abi Talib was a cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet Muhammad and the fourth caliph to rule the Muslim world. His followers were the original Shia Muslims, who regard him as the first rightful caliph.... [more]

Ali 2.desc: Diminutive of Alison, Alexandra and other names beginning with the same sound.

Alia 1.desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic علياء (see Alya 1).

Alibrand.desc: From the Old German elements alles meaning "other, foreign" and brant meaning "fire, torch, sword".

Alice.desc: From the Old French name Aalis, a short form of Adelais, itself a short form of the Germanic name Adalheidis (see Adelaide). This name became popular in France and England in the 12th century. It was among the most common names in England until the 16th century, when it began to decline. It was revived in the 19th century.... [more]

Alícia.desc: Catalan form of Alice, as well as a Portuguese variant.

Alik.desc: Diminutive of Aleksandr, Albert and other names beginning with the same sound.

Alikhan.desc: Combination of the name Ali 1 and the Turkic title khan meaning "ruler, leader".

Aliki.desc: Greek form of Alice. It also corresponds with the Greek word άλικη meaning "scarlet".

Alimjan.desc: Uyghur elaboration of Alim using the suffix جان (jan) meaning "dear, darling" (of Persian origin).

Alin.desc: Possibly a Romanian masculine form of Alina. Alternatively it may derive from Romanian alina "to soothe".

Alina.desc: Short form of Adelina, Albina and names that end in alina.

Alinafe.desc: Means "he or she is with us" in Chewa.

Aline.desc: Medieval short form of Adeline. As an English name, in modern times it has sometimes been regarded as a variant of Eileen. This was the name of a popular 1965 song by the French singer Christophe.

Alinur.desc: From the given name Ali 1 combined with Arabic نور (nur) meaning "light".

Aliona.desc: Alternate transcription of Russian Алёна or Ukrainian Альона (see Alyona).

Alireza.desc: Combination of Ali 1 and Reza, given in honour of the 9th-century Shia imam Ali ar-Ridha.

Alisa.desc: Form of Alice used in several languages.

Alisher.desc: From the given name Ali 1 combined with Persian شیر (sher) meaning "lion". It was borne by the 15th-century Timurid poet Ali-Shir Nava'i, who wrote in the Chagatai Turkic language.

Alison.desc: Norman French diminutive of Aalis (see Alice). It was common in England, Scotland and France in the Middle Ages, and was later revived in England in the 20th century via Scotland. Unlike most other English names ending in son, it is not derived from a surname.

Alix.desc: Medieval French variant of Alice, also sometimes used as a masculine name. This is the name of the hero (a young Gaulish man) of a French comic book series, which debuted in 1948.

Aliya 1.desc: Kazakh and Tatar form of Aliyah 1, as well as an alternate transcription of Arabic عليّة (see Aliyah 1).

Aliya 2.desc: Means "ascent" in Hebrew, a derivative of עָלָה ('alah) meaning "to ascend, to climb". This is also a Hebrew word referring to immigration to Israel.

Aliyah 2.desc: Alternate transcription of Hebrew עֲלִיָּה (see Aliya 2).

Aliyya.desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic عليّة (see Aliyah 1).

Aliyyah.desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic عليّة (see Aliyah 1).

Aljaž.desc: Derived from a Slovene surname, which is of unknown meaning.

Aljoša.desc: Slovene, Croatian and Serbian form of Alyosha. In Slovene it can also be a feminine name.

Alla.desc: Meaning unknown, possibly of German origin.

Allah.desc: Derived from Arabic الإله (al-ilah) meaning "the deity". It is primarily used to refer to the Islamic God, though it was originally used by pre-Islamic Arabs, and is sometimes used by Arabic-speaking Christians and Jews.

Allan.desc: Variant of Alan. The American author Edgar Allan Poe (1809-1849) got his middle name from the surname of the parents who adopted him.

Allegra.desc: Means "cheerful, lively" in Italian. It was borne by a short-lived illegitimate daughter of Lord Byron (1817-1822).

Allen.desc: Variant of Alan, or from a surname that was derived from this same name. A famous bearer of this name was Allen Ginsberg (1926-1997), an American beat poet. Another is the American film director and actor Woody Allen (1935-), who took the stage name Allen from his real first name.

Alli.desc: Finnish diminutive of names beginning with Al. This is also the Finnish word for a type of duck.

Allie.desc: Diminutive of Alison, Alexandra and other names beginning with the same sound. After a 34-year absence from the American top 1000 chart this name began growing in popularity after the premiere of the sitcom Kate and Allie in 1984.

Allison.desc: From the middle of the 20th century this has primarily been used as a variant of the feminine name Alison. However, prior to that it was used as an uncommon masculine name, derived from the English and Scottish surname Allison.

Allon.desc: Means "oak" in Hebrew. This name is mentioned briefly in the Old Testament.

Ally 1.desc: Diminutive of Alison, Alexandra and other names beginning with the same sound. This name jumped in popularity in 1997 after the premiere of the American television series Ally McBeal.

Allyn.desc: Variant or feminine form of Alan.

Alma 1.desc: This name became popular after the Battle of Alma (1854), which took place near the River Alma in Crimea and ended in a victory for Britain and France. However, the name was in rare use before the battle; it was probably inspired by Latin almus "nourishing". It also coincides with the Spanish word meaning "the soul".

Alma 3.desc: Meaning unknown. According to the Book of Mormon, this was the name of two prophets, father and son. Alma the Elder was a corrupt priest who repented after meeting the prophet Abinadi. Alma the Younger rebelled against the church, but repented and become a missionary and prophet.

Almantas.desc: From the Lithuanian root al- "all, every" combined with mantus "intelligent" or manta "property, wealth".

Almas.desc: Means "diamond" in Arabic, ultimately from Persian الماس (almas).

Almast.desc: Means "diamond" in Armenian, ultimately from Persian الماس (almas).

Almazbek.desc: From Kyrgyz алмаз (almaz) meaning "diamond", ultimately from Persian الماس (almas), combined with the Turkic military title beg meaning "chieftain, master".

Almira 1.desc: Variant of Elmira 1. Handel used it for the title character in his opera Almira (1705).

Almiro.desc: Meaning uncertain, possibly a masculine form of Almira 1.

Álmos.desc: Possibly from Hungarian álom "dream", though perhaps of Turkic origin meaning "bought". This was the name of the semi-legendary father of Árpád, the founder of the Hungarian state. Álmos's mother Emese supposedly had a dream in which a turul bird impregnated her and foretold that her son would be the father of a great nation.

Almudena.desc: Derived from Arabic المدينة (al-mudaynah) meaning "the citadel". It was in a building by this name that a concealed statue of the Virgin Mary was discovered during the Reconquista in Madrid. The Virgin of Almudena, that is Mary, is the patron saint of Madrid.

Alodia.desc: Possibly from a Visigothic name, maybe from Gothic elements such as alls "all" or aljis "other" combined with auds "riches, wealth". Saint Alodia was a 9th-century Spanish martyr with her sister Nunilo.

Alois.desc: German and Czech form of Aloysius.

Alojz.desc: Slovene, Slovak and Croatian form of Aloysius.

Alojzija.desc: Slovene and Croatian feminine form of Aloysius.

Alonzo.desc: Variant of Alonso in use in America.

Aloysius.desc: Latinized form of Aloys, an old Occitan form of Louis. This was the name of a 16th-century Italian saint, Aloysius Gonzaga. The name has been in occasional use among Catholics since his time.

Alparslan.desc: From Turkish alp meaning "brave" and arslan meaning "lion", referring to the 11th-century Seljuk sultan Alp Arslan, who expanded the Seljuk Empire into Anatolia.

Alperen.desc: From Turkish alp "hero" and eren "holy person".

Alpha.desc: From the name of the first letter in the Greek alphabet, Α.

Alphaeus.desc: From Ἀλφαῖος (Alphaios), the Greek form of a Hebrew name that meant "changing". In the New Testament this is the name of the fathers of the apostles James and Levi.

Alphius.desc: Meaning unknown, possibly a variant of Alphaeus, or possibly from an Umbrian root meaning "white". This was the name of a 3rd-century saint who was martyred in Sicily.

Alphonsus.desc: Latinized form of the Gothic name *Aþalfuns (see Alfonso). This name was borne by Saint Alphonsus Liguori, an 18th-century Italian bishop who is regarded as a Doctor of the Church.

Alpin.desc: Anglicized form of the Scottish Gaelic name Ailpean, possibly derived from a Pictish word meaning "white". This was the name of two kings of Dál Riata and two kings of the Picts in the 8th and 9th centuries.

Alta.desc: Possibly from Latin altus or Italian/Spanish alto meaning "high".

Altagracia.desc: Means "high grace", taken from the Spanish title of the Virgin Mary Nuestra Señora de la Altagracia, meaning "Our Lady of High Grace". She is considered the patron saint of the Dominican Republic, and it is there that this name is most often used.

Altair.desc: Means "the flyer" in Arabic. This is the name of a star in the constellation Aquila.
